analysis.investment_thesis: Mastek is a reasonably priced mid-tier IT services business with consistent FCF generation and a 9-year net profit CAGR of 32.5%, trading at an attractive 12.8x P/E with a ~9.5% FCF yield. However, IT services lacks the durable pricing power and wide moat I require — it is a people-intensive, competitive business where customers can and do switch vendors.
key_strengths: Attractive valuation: 12.8x P/E, 9.8x EV/EBITDA, with FCF of INR 515 Cr yielding ~9.5% on market cap
Consistent FCF generation — positive all 5 years (276→515 Cr), low capex intensity (~20-37 Cr/yr)
Conservative balance sheet: D/E 0.20, borrowings declining from 583 Cr (2025) to 438 Cr (2026), strong equity base of 2,992 Cr
key_risks: No durable moat: IT services is commoditized and competitive — pricing power is limited and talent-dependent
UK/government concentration: significant UK public sector exposure creates macro and policy risk (Brexit aftermath, budget cuts)
Net profit growth has plateaued: 310→311→376→404 Cr over FY23-26, far below the 32% 9-year CAGR, signaling maturation
red_flags: Finance costs exploded from INR 8 Cr (FY22) to INR 44 Cr (FY24) — the FY23 acquisition (INR 719 Cr investing outflow) added material debt
ROE of 15.6% is only barely above my 15% threshold and may compress further as the equity base grows faster than earnings
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Mastek is a competent, well-managed mid-tier IT services company with a commendable long-term track record — revenue compounding at 23% and net profit at 32% over nine years is genuinely impressive. The valuation at 12.8x trailing and 11.3x forward P/E is not expensive, and the FCF generation (INR 515 Cr on INR 5,412 Cr market cap) is the most attractive feature here. The balance sheet is clean with D/E of 0.20, and the company is actively paying down the acquisition-related debt taken on in FY23. For a value-oriented investor, the numbers superficially check many boxes.

The fundamental problem is moat. IT services is a labor-arbitrage business dressed up in digital transformation language. Mastek has carved a niche in Oracle Cloud implementations and UK public sector — these create some switching costs, but not the type of durable competitive advantage I require. The moment a competitor undercuts on price or a key account manager leaves, the business erodes. Operating margins at 14.1% are decent but not exceptional, and ROE at 15.6% barely clears my threshold. This is a fair business at a fair price — I'd rather own a wonderful business at a fair price. I would not initiate a new position, but existing holders need not panic given the valuation support.
